column1: Top left. Manufacturing, NACE section C. CN = NBS value added for firms above the revenue threshold, 2011–12 bridged via UNIDO; published corrections put its 2025 value at 233–296. Top right. NACE divisions 17, 19, 20, 23, 24 (paper, refining, chemicals, non-metallic minerals, basic metals). DE = Destatis Energieintensive Industriezweige; UK constructed to the same definition from ONS division indices (band = three weighting variants); CN = chemicals, minerals, ferrous and non-ferrous on 2007 value-added weights, excluding paper and refining (band = revenue weights). Bottom left. The same without chemicals and refining: divisions 17, 23, 24. UK chained on ONS weights (band = three weighting variants); DE = Eurostat division indices on Destatis production-index weights; CN = non-metallic minerals, ferrous and non-ferrous metals (band = revenue weights). Bottom right. Production tonnage of crude steel, primary aluminium, cement and paper & paperboard, each indexed to 2010 and combined on one set of weights for all three countries: EU27 value added for the matching NACE classes in 2010 (steel 44%, paper 28%, aluminium 15%, cement 13%). Band = three weightings: the same weights as an arithmetic and as a geometric mean, plus a set that trims aluminium to the primary-only share of its class. Sources. ONS, Destatis, Eurostat sts_inpr_a, Destatis weights, NBS, UNIDO; bottom right: steel from worldsteel; aluminium and cement from BGS World Mineral Production and USGS Minerals Yearbook; paper from FAOSTAT; China from the NBS Statistical Yearbook; weights from Eurostat structural business statistics.
